profile.stagger_pattern: NOT staggered. All five at-large council seats are elected concurrently every four years (2018, 2022, 2026) on the August ballot, as a single 'VOTE FOR 5' contest. Verified against the Putnam County Election Commission summary reports: Cookeville council races appear on the 2018-08-02, 2022-08-04 and 2026-08-06 ballots and are ABSENT from the 2020-08-06 and 2024-08-01 ballots (which carry Algood, Baxter and Monterey municipal races but no Cookeville contest). 2019-2021, 2023-2025 are therefore holdover years with no Cookeville city election at all - a structural fact, not a gap.

run_log.detail: Registry entries confirmed: (a) TN state hosts irrelevant here - never touched sos.tn.gov/elections.tn.gov; (b) Putnam County Election Commission fetches cleanly by curl, and the working pattern is https://putnamcountytn.gov/electionresults/{YYYY}-{MM}/ (the year-month index path was discovered from a single href on the county home page; the /electionresults/ root itself 403s). Server-rendered HTML summary reports, all municipal contests included. (c) mtas.tennessee.edu/directories/cities/cookeville fetched fine and gave the current roster plus 'Next Election 08-06-2026', confirming the August/even calendar - but as the registry warns it carries no term dates.

Registry said 'Cookeville Aug/even', implying 2018/2020/2022/2024/2026. That is only half right and the correction matters: Cookeville is QUADRENNIAL. The Putnam County summary reports for 2018-08-02, 2022-08-04 and 2026-08-06 each carry a single 'City Council City of Cookeville / Councilman-City Of Cookeville' contest marked VOTE FOR 5; the 2020-08-06 and 2024-08-01 reports carry Algood, Baxter and Monterey municipal races but NO Cookeville contest. All five at-large seats therefore turn over together every four years and 2019-2021, 2023-2025 are holdover years.

2018 (VOTE FOR 5): Shelton 3805, Wheaton 2904, Miller 2740, Walker 2691, Womack 2612 elected; Henry 2538 and Crabtree 1620 lost. 2022 (VOTE FOR 5): Wheaton 2433, Eldridge 1811, Walker 1747, Bagci 1642, Gilbert 1587 elected; incumbent Mark Miller 1397 finished 6th and was defeated, and Shelton and Womack did not appear on the ballot. 2026 (VOTE FOR 5): Gilbert 3269, Eldridge 3173, Cigi England 2770, Bagci 2654, Kelly McCorkle Parkison 2508 elected; Wheaton and Walker were not candidates. NOTE the '(I)' prefix on every 2026 name is a party/independent label, not an incumbency marker - it appears on candidates who have never held office.

AgendaCenter technique confirmed on cookeville-tn.gov and worth recording precisely. /AgendaCenter/ViewFile/ArchivedMinutes/_MMDDYYYY-{N} serves PDFs to plain curl and the date segment IS cosmetic - every document below was pulled with the literal segment _01012020. But the integer space is NOT chronological here: it interleaves City Council, Planning Commission, BZA and Historic Zoning documents from 2006 to 2026 in upload order, is sparse (roughly half of ids 1-700 return 404), and ids 1-13 and 626-637 return the AgendaCenter HTML page rather than a PDF. A full sweep of ids 1-700 with local pdftotext extraction produced ~30 dated City Council roll calls. Current-year meetings use a different type segment and a different id space: /AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_07162026-799.

About a third of the archived council minutes are image-only Canon scans that pdftotext returns empty. OCR path used: pdftoppm -r 200 -f 1 -l 1 -png, then tesseract <png> - --psm 4 -c preserve_interword_spaces=1. IMPORTANT LOCAL QUIRK: some of these scans are fed upside-down and need `sips -r 180` before OCR, while others are correctly oriented and are DESTROYED by that rotation (output comes back mirrored - 'ssaulsng ON' for 'No Business'). Try both orientations and keep the readable one. This recovered the two decisive documents: id 383 = August 18, 2022 (old council) and id 388 = September 1, 2022 (new council), which date the handover exactly.

MANDATORY check run and the answer is genuinely negative: ZERO mid-term changes 2019-2026. Roll calls were read at 2020-04-02, 2020-05-21, 2020-06-18, 2020-10-01, 2021-01-21, 2021-06-03, 2021-06-10, 2021-06-17, 2021-06-25, 2021-07-01, 2021-08-05, 2022-02 (id 369), 2022-08-18 - all Shelton/Wheaton/Miller/Walker/Womack with Shelton mayor and Wheaton vice-mayor; and 2022-09-01, 2023-05-18, 2023-06-01, 2023-07-20, 2023-10-05, 2023-11-16, 2023-12-07, 2024-02-01, 2024-03-21, 2024-04-04, 2024-06-06, 2025-04-17, 2025-05-15, 2025-06-05, 2025-06-19, 2025-07-17, 2025-09-18, 2025-10-02, 2025-12-18, 2026-01-15, 2026-05-07, 2026-05-21, 2026-07-16 - all Wheaton(mayor)/Eldridge(vice-mayor)/Bagci/Gilbert/Walker. No appointment, resignation, death or vacancy appears anywhere in the window, and the structural tell (an off-cycle race or a seat on two consecutive ballots) is absent because there were no intervening ballots at all.

Mayor determination handled as the city block demanded: Cookeville is council-manager, the mayor and vice-mayor are internal offices never on the ballot, and the election record alone would have made Shelton (top vote-getter 2018) and Wheaton (top vote-getter 2022) look like elected mayors by coincidence. They are in fact the council's choices - sourced from the roll-call titles in minutes on both sides of the 2022-09-01 organizational meeting. Day-of-week checks: 2018-08-02, 2022-08-04, 2026-08-06 are all Thursdays (TN August election day); 2022-08-18, 2022-09-01 and 2026-07-16 are Thursdays, matching the council's 1st/3rd-Thursday schedule. Two OCR/scan date traps caught and discarded: cached header dates '2028-07-01' (id 292) and '2024-07-31' (id 299) are misreads of 2021 documents whose bodies read June 25, 2021 and August 5, 2021 - the roll calls in both are roster A, which is internally consistent.

CAVEATS, filed here rather than as gaps. (1) No City Council roll call dated in calendar 2019 survives in the archive - the surviving 2019 documents are Board of Zoning Appeals (id 126, 2019-09-12) and planning items. The 2019 seat-years are nevertheless sourced by the 2018 county canvass (a fixed four-year term with no intervening election) and bracketed by roll calls before and after; council seats are recorded high, and the Mayor/Vice-Mayor rows for that stretch are recorded medium because an internal office could in principle have changed without an election. (2) Term-start boundary 2018-09-06 is INFERRED from the observed 2022 pattern (new council seated at the first regular meeting in September, verified 2022-08-18 old / 2022-09-01 new); it falls outside the panel window and affects no seat-year. (3) The 2026 winners England and McCorkle Parkison get NO tenure rows: winning is not holding. The August 6, 2026 council meeting - held on election day - still shows the outgoing council, minutes for 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-13 are not yet posted (404), and no source yet shows the new members seated. On the 2022 precedent the seating meeting would be 2026-09-03, which is after this run. For the same reason Wheaton's and Walker's rows are left ongoing even though neither stood for re-election.

Every seat-year 2019-2026 covered: 5 at-large council seat-years per year (40), plus Mayor (8) and Vice-Mayor (8) = 56 cells, zero gaps, zero known-vacant. Seat labels are undifferentiated 'At-Large' by design: all five seats are filled in one at-large VOTE FOR 5 contest with no positions, wards or numbering, so there is no seat identity to assign and inventing one would be fabrication.
